explanation: Let me describe the important physical ideas. Circular motion requires a net force toward the center, not an outward force. An inanimate surface exerts a normal contact force on an object it supports. Gravity acts in a vacuum and continues to pull downward throughout a ball’s flight. Velocity and acceleration can point in opposite directions, and zero velocity does not imply zero acceleration. Static friction opposes relative slipping at a contact, so it can point in the direction of an object’s motion. Net force causes acceleration, not velocity. An object keeps a constant velocity when the net force is zero. After release, a thrown object carries no stored force from the thrower. In a vacuum, objects fall with the same acceleration regardless of mass. Two interacting objects exert equal and opposite forces on each other, regardless of their masses.
